newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico summons NY Times journalist over drug story.
newsitem.headline: Mexico summons NY Times journalist over drug story.

text.p: Mexican authorities summoned a New York Times journalist for questioning on Friday in a criminal investigation over a story alleging two Mexican governors were linked to the drug trade.
The journalist, Sam Dillon, the Times' Mexico bureau chief, co-authored the Feb. 23 article based on U.S. intelligence reports.
The article said U.S. agents have linked Morelos state Gov. Jorge Carrillo Olea and Sonora state Gov. Manilo Fabio Beltrones to drug trafficking.
The two governors, who have strongly denied any drug ties, have asked prosecutors to bring charges against Dillon.
Dillon has not been charged with any crime.
In Mexico if a person is charged with defamation they can face up to two years in jail.
"We consider this law and this complaint attacks the rights of all journalists", Dillon told reporters. "The story is truthful. It was written in a very objective way".
Dillon's co-author, a U.S.-based colleague, Craig Pyes, lives outside Mexico.

Dillon said the Times' four-month investigation for the story was based largely on documents from a U.S. intelligence centre in El Paso, Texas, that is run by the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and coordinates intelligence reports from several different cities.
